correctness.rationale: Directly checked the actual source theorem, 2-inner-product quotient, and proof inequality. For any t in (0,1), r=(1-t)/(1+t), lambda=mu=t, p=(e1,0,...), q=(r e1,0,...), K=I, the source perturbation inequality reduces to 1-r=t(1+r) on the sole active index and vanishes on all other subsets. Its printed lower bound A_p min{1,((1-t)/(1-t))^2}=1 contradicts the q-only weave energy r^2. Triangle inequality instead gives (1+mu)sqrt(Eq)>= (1-lambda)sqrt(Ep), hence sharp corrected lower bound A_p min{1,((1-lambda)/(1+mu))^2}, attained by the family. No necessity or all-geometry optimality claim.

originality.rationale: The formula with 1+mu appears already as an inequality IN the source proof, so a corrected factor by itself is not newly proved here. The new scientifically distinct contribution is a source-specific parametric counterexample to the printed quantitative theorem and an exact optimality witness; no inspected independent correction or erratum establishes it. Closely related K-frame perturbation counterexamples use other source theorems and do not imply this example under the same hypotheses.
residual_risks: The original published proof itself states the corrected 1+mu factor; novelty is only the precise counterexample/correction and sharp witness, not rediscovery of its inequality.
A nonindexed corrigendum or author clarification may have supplied the same witness.

value.rationale: The printed statement promises a lower frame constant one, but the same perturbation hypotheses permit the q-only lower constant ((1-t)/(1+t))^2 tending to zero. Thus the unsupported stability claim can be arbitrarily inaccurate, and the corrected sharp universal quantitative guarantee resolves an explicit defect in published perturbation theory.
